one_liner: Rust Jsonnet interpreter, CLI and libjsonnet-compatible library; 1.9x to thousands of times faster than C++ jsonnet.
what_it_does: jrsonnet evaluates Jsonnet (the JSON templating language used for Kubernetes, Grafana and CI configs) to JSON/YAML/TOML. It ships as Rust crates (jrsonnet-evaluator plus jrsonnet-stdlib), a `jrsonnet` CLI, a C ABI shared/static library built from bindings/jsonnet that mimics google/jsonnet's libjsonnet.so (jsonnet_make, jsonnet_evaluate_file/snippet, _multi and _stream variants), WASM bindings on JSR/NPM and Python bindings (rjsonnet). Default builds implement standard Jsonnet; experimental syntax (destructuring, preserved field order, object iteration, null coalescing, bigint) is opt-in through cargo features.
how_it_is_fast: The evaluator works directly on the parsed IR with lazy thunks, interned strings (jrsonnet-interner IStr), FxHash maps and a reference-counted cycle collector (jrsonnet-gcmodule Cc), and the CLI is built with fat LTO, one codegen unit, panic=abort and mimalloc. Most of the largest gaps come from the standard library: jrsonnet implements 159 std builtins natively in Rust, while C++ jsonnet at the benchmarked revision defines std.sort, std.base64Decode, std.manifestTomlEx, std.parseInt and std.foldl in Jsonnet in stdlib/std.jsonnet. Current master also adds a static-analysis pass that resolves locals to numeric slots and marks which object fields depend on self/super so independent nested objects are built once; that pass did not exist at the benchmarked commit 4824700.
when_to_use: Rendering large real-world Jsonnet trees (kube-prometheus, Grafana/Mimir/Loki manifests, CI generators) where C++ jsonnet takes minutes to hours and go-jsonnet takes about a second: GraalVM CI 34.4 ms vs Go 600.3 ms, kube-prometheus 43.6 ms vs Go 1,068.4 ms.
Configs heavy on std builtins (sort, foldl, base64, manifestTomlEx, string joins), where C++ jsonnet's Jsonnet-level stdlib is 70x to 4,000x slower in the repo's tables.

Short CLI invocations in build pipelines: on the small-input rows jrsonnet's whole-process time is about 0.75-0.92 ms against 1.4-5.4 ms for Go, 1.8-3.0 ms for sjsonnet's native images and 16 ms or more for C++.
Rust services that want to embed Jsonnet as a library, or C/C++ programs that currently link libjsonnet.so and only use the evaluate entry points.
when_not_to_use: Workloads dominated by deep object-inheritance recursion or lazy arrays: sjsonnet native beats it on Inheritance recursion (46.7 vs 160.1 ms), Simple recursive call (18.0 vs 35.8 ms) and Comparison for primitives (174.8 vs 218.1 ms), and rsjsonnet beats it on Lazy array (10.7 vs 54.8 ms), Inheritance recursion (115.6 ms) and base64 of byte arrays.

Teams that need a stable, packaged release: crates.io stable and Homebrew are still 0.4.2 (issue #231 asks for a release supporting jsonnet 0.22.0), and the benchmarked code is a git build labelled 0.5.0-pre97; the newest prerelease is 0.5.0-pre98 (2026-05-05).

C/C++ embedders that rely on libjsonnet's GC tuning, custom allocators or error returns: jsonnet_gc_min_objects and jsonnet_gc_growth_trigger are no-ops, jsonnet_realloc assumes a 16-byte old allocation and is documented in its own comment as 'most definitely broken' (safe only with a malloc-style allocator), invalid arguments panic and release builds abort, and the library is publish = false, so it must be built from source.

Programs that need multiple independent VMs on different threads with different stack limits: evaluator state is Rc/RefCell and thread-local, and jsonnet_max_stack sets a global depth limit, ignoring its VM argument.

integration.form: crate (jrsonnet-evaluator, jrsonnet-stdlib) plus CLI binary; C ABI cdylib/staticlib (libjsonnet) built from bindings/jsonnet
integration.dependencies: jrsonnet-gcmodule, jrsonnet-interner, rustc-hash, stacker, smallvec, serde/serde_json, hi-doc (default explaining-traces feature), md5/sha1/sha2/sha3 for std hashing; mimalloc optional for the CLI
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2024 (Rust 1.85 or newer); README says latest stable and gives no MSRV policy
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 and aarch64 (benchmark derivations), macOS (Homebrew), Windows (flake cross-build), WASM (JSR/NPM package)
integration.thread_safety: Single-threaded per evaluator (Rc/RefCell state, thread-local STATE); libjsonnet's default interop-threading feature lets a VM move between threads, not share one
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — libjsonnet.so C API (evaluate_file/snippet, multi, stream; reports v0.22.0) is implemented for C/C++ hosts, but GC tuning calls are no-ops, jsonnet_realloc and panic behaviour differ, and experimental syntax is only on when built with exp-* features

gotchas: Harness: hyperfine runs with --output=pipe, so outputs of the six implementations are never compared (only a non-zero exit fails a run), and every binary is launched through a nix makeWrapper shell wrapper that adds --max-stack 200000, so the microsecond rows (jrsonnet floor about 750-920 us: Tail call, String strips, Big object, manifestJsonEx, manifestTomlEx, parseInt, substr) measure process plus wrapper startup more than evaluation.

The headline >50x ratios against C++ (Array sorts 1,531x, base64Decode 4,069x, manifestTomlEx 692x, Inheritance function recursion 1,061x) compare native Rust builtins with C++ jsonnet's Jsonnet-level stdlib. Over the 18 rows C++ completed, the geomean is about 70x, but on the six evaluator-bound rows (Tail call, Inheritance recursion, Simple recursive call, Lazy array, Big object, Large string join) it is about 7.6x, ranging 1.89x to 21.3x (derived from page data). C++ was skipped on the real-world rows as taking hours.

Allocator and build asymmetry: jrsonnet is measured with --features=mimalloc and fat LTO, C++ jsonnet with its Makefile's g++ -O3 and glibc malloc; embedding through libjsonnet uses the host's allocator, so library users may not see the CLI numbers.

Master has moved past the benchmarked commit (static analysis pass added; issue #239, opened 2026-10-06, reports State::import_resolved leaving a file marked 'evaluating' after a static analysis error), and the doc still uses sjsonnet 0.6.2 (issue #234 asks for a rerun with 0.7.0).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against sjsonnet, the catalogued sibling for the same workload, pick jrsonnet when you want a single native binary or a C ABI with no JVM: it is 1.9x to 4.7x faster on the real-world rows (GraalVM CI 34.4 vs 65.1-69.6 ms, kube-prometheus 43.6 vs 183.7-204.6 ms). Prefer sjsonnet only when inheritance-recursion-heavy configs dominate or a JVM is already in the stack.
verified_claims_summary: With hyperfine (-N, 4 warm-ups, at least 20 runs) on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D and nix-pinned toolchains, a jrsonnet git build (fat LTO, mimalloc) beat C++ jsonnet v0.22.0-rc1 (g++ -O3 via its Makefile) on all 18 rows C++ finished, from 1.89x (Lazy array) and 2.20x (Simple recursive call) up to 4,069x (base64Decode), and beat go-jsonnet v0.22.0-rc1 17.5x on GraalVM CI and 24.5x on kube-prometheus, where C++ was not run. All timings are whole-process wall time, and outputs were not compared.
status_note: Actively maintained by a single author (last commit 2026-08-31, about 1.2M crates.io downloads of jrsonnet-evaluator), MIT-licensed and packaged in nixpkgs and Homebrew. Packaged stable releases lag at 0.4.2, so getting the benchmarked performance means building from git or using a 0.5.0 prerelease.
